about: This part finishes the second bardo and opens the third. Whoever misses the first clear light at death meets a second, in a body made of mind, at a moment when he cannot tell whether he has died; if he recognises it then, he is freed before the visions of karma begin. If not, the bardo of reality dawns. The dead man sees his relatives weeping, his share of food cut off and his clothes taken away; he sees them and hears them call, but they cannot see or hear him, and he goes away unhappy. Sounds, lights and rays appear and terrify him. Now the reader gives the Great Pointing-Out: he names the six bardos, tells the dead man that he has died and that clinging to this life is useless, and gives him six lines of verse to say to himself. The sounds, lights and rays are the radiance of his own reality, and a body made of mind cannot be harmed or die. After three and a half days unconscious he wakes into the bardo, and the first day begins: the sky turns blue, and from the central realm the white buddha Vairocana appears in union with his consort. The blinding blue light of the wisdom of the expanse of reality pierces toward the dead man, and with it the dull white light of the gods. He will fear the bright light and be drawn to the dull one; he is told to trust the bright light and pray to it.

sentences.w: བར་དོ་ དང་པོ་ ཐེབས་ ན་ རབ༔ དེ་ མ་ ཐེབས་ ན་ བར་དོ་ གཉིས་པ་ ལ་ གསལ་གདབ་བས༔ རིགས་ སད་ ནས་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ།
sentences.l: The between first took-hold if, best. That not took-hold if, the between second in clear-reminding-by, the family(?) having-woken, then, freed it-is.
sentences.i: If it takes hold in the first bardo, that is best. If it does not, he is reminded in the second bardo, and by that what is in him by nature wakes, and he is freed.
sentences.n: The first words, bar do, stand at the end of p. 26, after the last sentence of the part before. bar do dang po thebs na rab: 'if it takes hold in the first bardo, best'; rab, 'best', as in the pilot's 'pho ba thebs na rab. The syllables pa la are uncertain: the print cuts them as one, པལ, either a contraction or pa la with its tsheg lost; the sense is pa la, 'in the second', either way, and it is written out. gdab bas is the print's spelling of gdab pas, 'by giving'. rigs, 'family, kind', is odd here: the other recension has rig pa sad nas, 'awareness wakes'. The print's rigs may stand for the same, or for the buddha-nature as one's 'family'; the translation is a guess. The plain stroke ། closes the sentence.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ བར་དོ་ གཉིས་པ་ མ་ དག་པའི་ སྒྱུ་ལུས་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ༔ ཤིའམ་ མ་ ཤི་ ངོ་ མི་ ཤེས་པའི་ གསལ་ ལམ་པ་ གཅིག་ འོང་༔
sentences.l: That too: the between second, impure's illusory-body so-called: died-or not died, face not knowing's clear flash, one, comes.
sentences.i: This second bardo is called the impure illusory body. There comes a flash of clarity in which the dead person does not know whether he has died or not.
sentences.n: sgyu lus, 'illusory body', is the body one seems to have after death, made of mind, not flesh; ma dag pa'i, 'impure', sets it apart from the pure illusory body of an accomplished yogin. shi'am ma shi, 'died, or not died', is the question of 002 put shortly: -'am is 'or'. gsal lam pa, 'a clear flash', makes a noun of the lam of 002's lam gyis, 'in a flash'; the other recension has shes pa gsal lam me ba, 'consciousness clear and flickering'. 'ong, 'comes', stands without a sentence ending, as it often does in this print.

sentences.w: དུས་ དེར་ གདམས་པ་ ཐེབས་ ན་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ མ་བུ་ འཕྲད་ ནས་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ ཁ་བསྒྱུར་དུ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Time at-that, the instruction took-hold if: reality-itself mother-child having-met, then, karma's turning-aside there-is-not.
sentences.i: If the instruction takes hold at that time, mother and child, the two clear lights of reality, meet, and karma can no longer turn him aside.
sentences.n: ma bu, 'mother and child', is a term of this teaching: the 'mother' is the clear light of reality itself, which dawns at death, and the 'child' is the clear light the practitioner came to know in meditation. Their meeting is recognition. kha bsgyur, 'to turn the face', is to divert, to turn aside; -du med, 'there is no ...-ing', says it cannot happen. las kyi, 'of karma', has the genitive where the other recension has las kyis, 'by karma', with the same sense.

sentences.w: དཔེར་ན་ ཉི་མའི་ འོད་ ཀྱི་ མུན་བ་ བཅོམ་པ་ བཞིན་དུ་ ལམ་ གྱི་ འོད་གསལ་ གྱིས་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ ནུས་པ་ བཅོམ་ ནས་ གྲོལ་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: For-example: the sun's light by darkness destroyed like, the path's clear-light by, karma's power having-destroyed, then, freed it-is.
sentences.i: Just as the light of the sun destroys darkness, the clear light of the path destroys the power of karma, and he is freed.
sentences.n: dper na, 'for example'. 'od kyi has kyi, 'of', where kyis, 'by', is meant, as the print often writes it; mun ba is its spelling of mun pa, 'darkness'. bcom, 'destroyed', is the past of 'joms. lam gyi 'od gsal, 'the clear light of the path', is the clear light as known in practice during life: the 'child' of the sentence before.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ བར་དོ་ གཉིས་པ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ ནི་ ཡིད་ ཀྱི་ ལུས་སུ་ ལམ་གྱིས་ འཆར་བ་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔ ཤེས་པ་ སྔར་ བཞིན་དུ་ ཐོ་ཡུག་ཏུ་ འཁོར་རོ༔
sentences.l: That too: the between second so-called, as-for: mind's body-as in-a-flash dawning it-is, and: consciousness, before like, around(?) circles.
sentences.i: What is called the second bardo is a dawning, in a flash, as a body made of mind. Consciousness wanders about as before.
sentences.n: yid kyi lus, 'body of mind', is the illusory body of the sentence before; lus su, 'as a body'. tho yug tu is uncertain: the other recension has mthong yul du, 'in the field of sight', and the print's tho yug may be a spelling of that or a word for 'all around'; 'wanders about' is a guess. 'khor ro, 'circles, goes round'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ གདམས་ངག་ འདི་ ཐེབས་ ན་ དོན་ འགྲུབ་ སྟེ༔ ད་དུང་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ འཁྲུལ་སྣང་ མ་ ཤར་བས་ གང་དུ་ ཡང་ བསྒྱུར་དུ་ བཏུབ་བོ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, instruction this took-hold if, the aim is-accomplished, and: still, karma's delusive-appearances not arisen-because, wherever-to even, turning is-possible.
sentences.i: If this instruction takes hold at that time, the aim is achieved: the deluded visions of karma have not yet arisen, so he can still be turned in any direction.
sentences.n: don 'grub, 'the aim is accomplished'; the other recension has don kun 'grub, 'every aim'. da dung, 'still, yet'. btub, 'can, is fit to', after bsgyur du, 'to turn': the dead person can still be steered. shar bas, 'because ... arisen', is shar with -pas, here spelled bas.

sentences.w: དེ་ལྟར་ གཞིའི་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོ་ མ་ འཕྲོད་ ཀྱང་༔ བར་དོ་ གཉིས་པའི་ འོད་གསལ་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་ དེ་ གྲོལ་ལོ༔
sentences.l: Thus, the ground's clear-light face not met though, the between second's clear-light face meeting, and, freed.
sentences.i: So even if he did not recognise the clear light of the ground, he recognises the clear light of the second bardo and is freed.
sentences.n: gzhi'i 'od gsal, 'the clear light of the ground', is the first clear light of 002, met at the moment of death. ngo 'phrod, 'the face meets', is this print's usual word for recognising; ngo ma 'phrod kyang, 'though it was not recognised'. de after 'phrod is te, 'and', in the form it takes after -d.

sentences.w: དེར་ ཡང་ མ་ གྲོལ་ ན༔ དེ་ནས་ བར་དོ་ གསུམ་པ་ ཡང་ ཟེར༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ འཆར་ དེ༔
sentences.l: There too not freed if: then, the between third also it-is-called: the reality-itself between dawns, and:
sentences.i: If he is not freed there either, then the bardo of reality dawns, which is also called the third bardo.
sentences.n: The print has མགྲོལ, a misprint for མ་གྲོལ, corrected here: the tsheg after ma is missing, and only ma grol, 'not freed', gives sense, as in the other recension (des kyang ma grol na). zer, 'it is called', is the spoken verb of 002. 'char de is the print's spelling of 'char te, 'dawns, and'. The chos nyid bar do, the bardo of reality, is where the peaceful and wrathful deities appear; the rest of the book is about it.

sentences.w: བར་དོ་ གསུམ་པ་ ལས་ ཀྱི་ འཁྲུལ་སྣང་ བྱ་བ་ ཤར་དུ་ འོང་བས༔ འདིའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོའི་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ ཆེན་མོ་ ཀློག་པ་ གལ་ཆེ་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: The between third: karma's delusive-appearances so-called arising comes-because, this's time-at, reality-itself between's great face-introduction reading important-is, and:
sentences.i: In the third bardo what are called the deluded visions of karma will arise, so at this time it is important to read the Great Pointing-Out of the bardo of reality.
sentences.n: bya ba, 'so-called', here without zhes. shar du 'ong, 'comes to arise', is 'will arise'; the other recension has 'char du 'ong. gal che, 'important' (literally 'the stake is great'). ngo sprod chen mo, 'the great pointing-out', is the name of the instruction that follows, the main part of the book.

sentences.w: སྟོབས་ དང་ ཕན་ཡོན་ ཤིན་ཏུ་ ཆེའོ༔
sentences.l: Power and benefit very great-are.
sentences.i: Its power and its benefit are very great.
sentences.n: phan yon, 'benefit, advantage'. che'o, 'are great': che with the sentence-ending -'o.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཉེ་དུས་ དུ་སྐད་ སྨྲེ་སྔགས་ འདོན་ ཟས་སྐལ་ བཅད༔ གོས་ བཤུས༔
sentences.l: At-that-time, by-relatives wailing(?), lament uttering, food-share cut, clothes stripped,
sentences.i: At that time his relatives are weeping and lamenting, his share of food has been stopped, his clothes taken off,
sentences.n: de tsa na, 'at that time'. nye dus is nye du, 'relatives', with -s, 'by', marking who does it. The print reads du skad, which gives no sense; it is kept as printed. It is almost certainly ngu skad, 'the sound of weeping', which the other recension has (compare du rgod in 002, kept for the same reason), and the translation takes it so. zas skal, 'food-share', the portion set aside for him at meals, now cut off. bshus, 'stripped'. These are the things the dead man sees being done around him.

sentences.w: མལ་ས་ འཆག་པ་ ལ་སོགས་ རང་ གིས་ ཁོང་ རྣམས་ མཐོང་ ཡང་༔ ཁོང་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས་ རང་ མ་ མཐོང་༔
sentences.l: Bed-place treading(?) and-so-on: oneself by them (plural) see though, they (plural) by oneself not see.
sentences.i: his bed trodden over, and so on. He sees them, but they do not see him.
sentences.n: mal sa, 'bed-place', where he lay. 'chag pa is uncertain: 'chag is 'to walk, to tread', and the print's word is kept; the other recension has mal sa phyags, 'they sweep the bed'. Whether the bed is trodden or cleared is a guess. la sogs, 'and so on'. rang, 'oneself', is the dead person, as in 002; khong rnams, 'they', is the polite third person with the plural.

sentences.w: ཁོང་ རྣམས་ ཀྱིས་ རང་ ལ་ བོས་བ་ ཐོས་ ཀྱང་༔ རང་ གི་ ཁོང་ རྣམས་ ལ་ བོས་བ་ མ་ ཐོས་བས༔ སྙིང་ མི་ དགའ་ ཕྱད་ དེ་ འགྲོའོ༔
sentences.l: They (plural) by oneself to calling hears though, oneself by them (plural) to calling not heard-because: heart not glad, (turning?), and, goes.
sentences.i: He hears them calling him, but they do not hear him calling them, and he goes away unhappy.
sentences.n: bos ba, 'calling', with the print's ba for pa. rang gi has gi for gis, 'by', the print's habit noted in the pilot. thos bas is its spelling of thos pas, 'because ... heard'. snying mi dga', 'the heart not glad', is 'sad'. phyad is uncertain: no verb phyad is known to fit; it may be a spelling of a verb of parting or turning away, and the translation passes over it. de after phyad is te, 'and'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ སྒྲ་ འོད་ ཟེར་ གསུམ་ གྱི་ སྣང་བ་ ཤར་ ནས༔ འཇིགས་ སྐྲག་ དངངས་ གསུམ་ གྱིས་ འོ་བརྒྱལ་ ནས་ འོངས་པས༔
sentences.l: That's time: sound, light, rays, three's appearances having-arisen, then; fear, terror, dread, three by, worn-out having-been, then, came-because:
sentences.i: At that time the visions of the three, sounds, lights and rays, arise, and he comes worn out by the three, fear, terror and dread. So
sentences.n: sgra 'od zer gsum, 'the three, sound, light and rays', come back again and again in what follows: 'od is light, zer the rays that stream from it. 'jigs skrag dngangs gsum, 'fear, terror and dread', are three near-synonyms; dngangs is the print's spelling of sngangs, 'to be terrified'. 'o brgyal, 'weary, worn out', where the other recension has brgyal, 'faints'. 'ongs pas, 'having come, therefore': the sentence runs on.

sentences.w: འདིའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོའི་ ངོ་སྤྲོད་ ཆེན་མོ་ གདབ་པར་ བྱ་ སྟེ༔ ཚེ་འདས་ ཀྱི་ མིང་ ནས་ བོས་ ལ་ སྒྲ་ དག་ ཅིང་ ཚིག་ གསལ་བར་ འདི་སྐད་དུ་ བཤད་དོ༔
sentences.l: This's time-at, reality-itself between's great face-introduction to-give is-to-be-done, and: the dead-one's by-name having-called, and, sound correct and words clearly, these-words-in say.
sentences.i: at this time the Great Pointing-Out of the bardo of reality should be given. Call the dead person by name and say this, pronouncing it correctly and with every word distinct:
sentences.n: gdab par bya, 'is to be given': the pilot's bya'o, here without its ending and followed by ste. tshe 'das kyi ming nas bos, 'calling the dead one by name'. sgra dag cing tshig gsal bar, 'the sound correct and the words clear', is the pilot's phrase with cing, 'and', for la. 'di skad du, 'in these words'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ མདུན་པ་ དྲག་པོས་ ཉོན་ཅིག༔ བར་དོ་ རྣམ་པ་ དྲུག་ ཡིན་ ཏེ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Not distracted-way, intention(?) fierce-by, listen! The between kinds six are, and:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, listen without distraction and with all your will. There are six kinds of bardo:
sentences.n: mdun pa drag pos, 'with a fierce intention': the print's mdun pa seems to stand for 'dun pa, 'aspiration, intent', which the other recension has; the sense is a guess. rnam pa drug, 'six kinds'.

sentences.w: རང་བཞིན་ སྐྱེས་གནས་ ཀྱི་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ རྨི་ལམ་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ ཏིང་ངེ་འཛིན་ བསམ་གཏན་ གྱི་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ ལུགས་འབྱུང་ སྲིད་པའི་ བར་དོ་ དེ་ དྲུག་གོ༔
sentences.l: Natural birth-place's the between, and; dream the between, and; absorption concentration's the between, and; dying-point's the between, and; reality-itself the between, and; in-order-arising(?) becoming's the between: those six.
sentences.i: the natural bardo of the place of birth, the bardo of dream, the bardo of meditative concentration, the bardo of the moment of death, the bardo of reality, and the bardo of becoming that arises in sequence: these are the six.
sentences.n: The six bardos. rang bzhin skyes gnas, 'the natural place of birth', is this life itself, from birth to death; skyes gnas is the print's spelling of skye gnas, which the other recension has. ting nge 'dzin (samādhi) and bsam gtan (dhyāna) are two words for meditative absorption. srid pa, 'becoming', names the bardo in which one seeks a new birth. lugs 'byung, 'arising in order', is a guess at the sense; both recensions have it. de drug go, 'those are the six'.

sentences.w: རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ བར་དོ་ གསུམ་ འབྱུང་ སྟེ༔ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ སྲིད་པ་ བར་དོ་ དང་ གསུམ་ འཆར་བ་ ལས༔
sentences.l: Child-of-noble-family! To you the betweens three occur, and: dying-point's the between, and; reality-itself the between, and; becoming the between, and, three dawning, of:
sentences.i: Child of noble family, three bardos come to you: the bardo of the moment of death, the bardo of reality and the bardo of becoming. Of these three that dawn,
sentences.n: 'byung, 'to come about, occur'. dang gsum, 'and (these) three': a list is closed with dang and the number. las after 'char ba is 'of, from among', and leads into the next sentence.

sentences.w: ཁ་སང་ ཕན་ཆད་ འཆི་ཁའི་ བར་དོ་ ལ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ འོད་གསལ་ ཤར་ ཡང་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱིས་ ངོས་ མ་ ཟིན་པས༔ འདིར་ འཁྱམས་ དགོས་ བྱུང་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: Yesterday up-to, the dying-point's between in, reality-itself clear-light arose though, you by recognition not seized-because: here to-wander must happened it-is.
sentences.i: until yesterday, in the bardo of the moment of death, the clear light of reality dawned, but you did not recognise it, and so you have had to wander here.
sentences.n: kha sang, 'yesterday'; phan chad, 'up to'. The dead person is spoken to as if a day or more has passed since death. 'khyams, 'to wander, roam'. dgos byung ba yin, 'it has come about that you must': byung, 'came about', makes the past.

sentences.w: ད་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ དང་༔ སྲིད་པ་ བར་དོ་ གཉིས་ འབྱུང་ སྟེ༔ བདག་ གིས་ ངོ་སྤྲད་བ་ རྣམས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ མ་ ཡེངས་པར་ ངོས་ ཟིན་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Now, as-for: to you, reality-itself the between and becoming the between, two, occur, and: by-me face-introduced-things (plural), you-yourself not distracted-way recognition seizing do!
sentences.i: Now the bardo of reality and the bardo of becoming, these two, come to you. Recognise without distraction what I point out to you.
sentences.n: The print writes gis after bdag at a line end as one letter with a small s under the g (གྶི), as in 002; it is written out. bdag, 'I', is the reader. ngo sprad ba, with sprad, the past and future stem of sprod, and the print's ba for pa, 'what is pointed out'; rnams makes it plural, 'the things I point out'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ད་ ནི་ འཆི་བ་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ དེ་ སླེབ་པ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Now, as-for: death so-called, that, arrived it-is.
sentences.i: O child of noble family, what is called death has now come.
sentences.n: sleb pa yin no, 'has arrived'. In 002 the same words were said before death: 'chi ba de 'ong bar 'dug, 'death seems to be coming'.

sentences.w: འཇིག་རྟེན་ འདི་ ནས་ ནི་ འགྲོ་ སྟེ༔ ཁྱོད་ ཅིག་པོ་ ནི་ མ་ ཡིན༔ ཀུན་ ལ་ འབྱུང་བས་ ཚེ་ འདི་ ལ་ ཆགས་པ་ དང་ ཞེན་པ་ ནི་ མ་ བྱེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: World this from, as-for, going, and: you alone, as-for, it-is-not. To-all happens-because: life this to, attachment and clinging, as-for, not do!
sentences.i: You are leaving this world. You are not the only one; it happens to all. So do not be attached to this life or cling to it.
sentences.n: 'jig rten, 'the perishable support', is 'the world'. khyod cig po, 'you alone', is the print's spelling of gcig pu. ni, three times in these lines, puts weight on the word before it: 'not you alone', 'attachment, that you must not do'. chags pa, 'attachment', and zhen pa, 'clinging', are near-synonyms paired for weight. ma byed cig, 'do not do': ma with the present stem byed and the particle cig forbids (the imperative of byed is gyis).

sentences.w: ཆགས་པ་ དང་ ཞེན་པ་ བྱས་ ཀྱང་ སྡོད་ དབང་ ནི་ མེད༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམས་པ་ ལས་ མི་ འོང་༔ མ་ ཆགས་ཤིག་ མ་ ཞེན་ཅིག༔ དཀོན་མཆོག་གསུམ་ དྲན་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Attachment and clinging done though, to-stay power, as-for, there-is-not. You-yourself in-saṃsāra wandering, other-than, not comes. Not be-attached! Not cling! Rare-Supreme-Three remembering do!
sentences.i: Even if you are attached and cling, you have no power to stay; nothing will come of it but wandering in saṃsāra. Do not be attached, do not cling. Keep the Three Jewels in mind.
sentences.n: sdod dbang, 'the power to stay'. byas kyang, 'even if (you) do', makes the clause concessive, where the other recension has byas cing, 'doing, and'. 'khor bar 'khyams pa las mi 'ong: las after a verb is 'other than', so 'nothing comes but wandering in saṃsāra'. 'khor ba, 'the round', is saṃsāra, the cycle of birth and death. dkon mchog gsum, 'the three rare and supreme ones', are the Three Jewels: the Buddha, his teaching and the community.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོའི་ སྣང་བ་ ལ་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ ཇི་ལྟར་ ཤར་ ནས་ བྱུང་ ཡང་༔ ཁྱོད་རང་ ཚིག་ འདི་ མ་ བརྗེད་པར་ གྱིས་ ལ་ ཚིག་དོན་ ཡིད་ ལ་ དྲན་ བཞིན་དུ་ སོང་ཞིག༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Reality-itself between's appearances at, terror however having-arisen happened though: you-yourself words these not forgetting do, and, words-meaning mind in remembering while, go!
sentences.i: O child of noble family, however much terror may arise at the visions of the bardo of reality, do not forget these words; go on with their meaning held in your mind.
sentences.n: ji ltar ... yang, 'however ... though'. shar nas byung, 'having arisen, came about', doubles the verb for weight. dran bzhin du, 'while remembering': bzhin du after a verb is 'while'. song zhig, the imperative of 'gro, 'go!'. tshig don, 'the words and their meaning'.

sentences.w: དེས་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་པའི་ གནད་ ཡོད་དོ༔
sentences.l: By-that, face-meeting's key-point there-is.
sentences.i: In that lies the key to recognition.
sentences.n: gnad, 'vital point', the place where a thing is decided, like a pressure point on the body. des, 'by that': remembering the words is what makes recognition possible.

sentences.w: ཀྱེ་མ་ བདག་ ལ་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ བར་དོ་ ཤར་ དུས་ འདིར༔ / ཀུན་ ལ་ དངངས་ སྐྲག་ འཇིགས་སྣང་ སྤངས་ བྱས་ ནས༔ / གང་ སྣང་ རང་ཤར་ རིག་པར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་ བྱ༔ / བར་དོའི་ སྣང་ཚུལ་ ཡིན་པར་ ཤེས་པར་ བྱ༔
sentences.l:
Alas! Me to, reality-itself between arising time this-at,
all toward, dread, terror, fearful-appearance abandonment having-made,
whatever appears, self-arisen, as-knowing face-know I-shall,
the between's way-of-appearing it-is, know I-shall.
sentences.i:
Alas! Now, when the bardo of reality dawns for me,
I shall give up all dread and terror, all fear of what appears,
and recognise whatever appears as awareness, arisen of itself;
I shall know it for the way the bardo appears.
sentences.n: Verse: six lines of nine syllables (the first with kye ma before it), which the dead person is to say to himself. The print writes dngangs with a small s under the second nga (དངངྶ); it is written out. The vowel of ngo in the third line cannot be seen apart from the letters of the line above; ngo shes, the set phrase, is the reading taken, and it is uncertain. 'jigs snang, 'fearful appearance'. spangs byas, 'made an abandoning', is 'having given up'. rang shar, 'arisen of itself'. rig par, 'as rig pa', awareness: what everything is to be recognised as. bya at the end of a line is 'I shall do': ngo shes bya, 'I shall recognise'. snang tshul, 'way of appearing'. Where this print has gang snang rang shar, 'whatever appears, self-arisen', the other recension has gang shar rang snang, 'whatever arises, self-appearing'.

sentences.w: དོན་ཆེན་ འགག་ ལ་ ཐུགས་པའི་ དུས་ཚོད་ འདིར༔ / རང་སྣང་ ཞི་ཁྲོའི་ ཚོགས་ ལ་ འཇིགས་ མི་ བྱ༔
sentences.l:
Great-matter crucial-point at reaching(?)'s time this-at,
self-appearance peaceful-wrathful's hosts toward, fear not I-shall-do.
sentences.i:
At this time when the great matter has come to its crucial point,
I shall not fear the hosts of the peaceful and wrathful, my own appearance.
sentences.n: don chen, 'the great matter'. 'gag, 'the crucial point', literally a narrow pass. The print has thugs pa'i, which gives no sense here (thugs is 'mind' in the respectful register); it is kept as printed, and read, as a guess, as thug pa'i, 'reaching', the set phrase 'gag la thug pa, which the other recension has. rang snang, 'self-appearance': what the mind itself shows. zhi khro, the peaceful and wrathful deities of the book's title. 'jigs mi bya, 'I shall not fear'.

sentences.w: དེ་སྐད་ ངག་ ནས་ ལྷང་ལྷང་ བརྗོད་ ལ༔ ཚིག་དོན་ ཡིད་ ལ་ དྲན་ བཞིན་དུ་ སོང་ཞིག༔
sentences.l: Those-words, speech-from, distinctly saying, and, words-meaning mind in remembering while, go!
sentences.i: Say these words aloud and distinctly, and go on with their meaning held in your mind.
sentences.n: ngag nas, 'from speech', aloud. lhang lhang, 'clearly, distinctly', a doubled word. The second clause repeats the words said just before the verse.

sentences.w: དེས་ འཇིགས་སྐྲག་ གི་ སྣང་པ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ ཤར་ ཡང་ རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངེས་པར་ ངོ་ འཕྲོད་པའི་ གནད་ ཡོད་པས་ མ་ བརྗེད་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: By-that: terror's appearances however arisen though, as-self-appearance certainly face-meeting's key-point there-is-because, not forget!
sentences.i: For in this lies the key: however terrifying the visions that arise, you will surely recognise them as your own appearance. Do not forget it.
sentences.n: snang pa is the print's spelling of snang ba, 'appearance'. rang snang du, 'as self-appearance'. ma brjed cig, 'do not forget!'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ ལུས་ དང་ སེམས་ བྲལ་བའི་ དུས་སུ༔ ཆོས་ཉིད་ དག་པའི་ སྣང་བ་ ཕྲ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ༔ གསལ་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ རང་བཞིན་ བཀྲག་ གསལ་ ལ་ ཉམས་ང་བ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family, your body and mind parted's time-at: reality-itself pure's appearance, subtle and clear, bright and shimmering, by-nature lustrous, bright and fearsome,
sentences.i: O child of noble family, when your body and mind part, the pure vision of reality, subtle and clear, bright and shimmering, lustrous and bright by nature, and fearsome,
sentences.n: The print writes phra la, 'subtle and', as one syllable (ཕྲལ); it is written out. la between two adjectives is 'and': phra la dwangs pa, gsal la 'tsher ba. bral, 'to part'. bkrag, 'lustre, brilliance'. nyams nga ba, 'fearsome, awesome', is the print's spelling of nyam nga ba. The other recension has no gsal after bkrag.

sentences.w: སོས་ཁའི་ ཐང་ ལ་ སྨིག་རྒྱུ་ བཞིན་ མེ་རེ་རེ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Spring's plain on mirage like, shimmering, dawning comes.
sentences.i: will dawn, quivering like a mirage on a plain in spring.
sentences.n: sos kha, 'spring', is the print's spelling of sos ka. smig rgyu, 'mirage'. me re re is a doubled-sound word for a flickering, quivering shimmer. 'char du 'ong ngo, 'comes to dawn': 'will dawn'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག་ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ དེ་ ནི་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ རང་མདངས་ ཡིན་པས་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That at, not fear! Not be-frightened! Not be-terrified! That, as-for, you-yourself's reality-itself's own-radiance it-is-because, face-knowing do!
sentences.i: Do not be afraid of it, do not be frightened, do not be terrified. It is the natural radiance of your own reality: recognise it.
sentences.n: Three prohibitions, ma 'jigs shig, ma skrag cig, ma dngangs shig, one for each of the three fears named above; here too the print writes dngangs with a small s under the second nga (དངངྶ), written out. rang mdangs, 'own radiance', the glow that reality itself gives off. khyod rang gi chos nyid, 'your own reality': it is not outside him.

sentences.w: འོད་ ཀྱི་ ནང་ ནས་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ རང་སྒྲ་ སྒྲ་ དག་ ལ་ ལྡིར་ ཆེ་བ༔ འབྲུག་ སྟོང་ དུས་ གཅིག་ ལ་ འདིར་ བཙམ་དུ་ དི་རི་རི་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Light's inside from, reality-itself's own-sound, sound pure(?) and roaring great, thunders thousand time one at roaring(?)-as-much-as, rumbling, comes.
sentences.i: From within the light comes the natural sound of reality, loud and roaring, rumbling like a thousand thunderclaps at once.
sentences.n: rang sgra, 'own sound', is like rang mdangs: the sound that reality itself makes. The print reads sgra dag la ldir che ba, 'the sound pure and greatly roaring'; the other recension has sgra drag, 'loud', with no repeated sgra, and the print's sgra dag may be a slip for it. It is kept, and the translation takes 'loud'. 'brug, 'dragon', is the Tibetan word for thunder. 'dir btsam du is kept as printed, though it gives no sense: it is probably ldir ba tsam du, 'as loud as the roaring of', which the other recension has, and the translation follows that guess. di ri ri is a rumbling sound.

sentences.w: དེ་ ཡང་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ ཆོས་ཉིད་ ཀྱི་ རང་སྒྲ་ ཡིན་པས༔ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ འཇིགས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་ཅིག༔ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That too, you-yourself's reality-itself's own-sound it-is-because: that at not fear! Not be-frightened! Not be-terrified!
sentences.i: That too is the natural sound of your own reality, so do not be afraid of it, do not be frightened, do not be terrified.
sentences.n: The same three prohibitions; here the print writes dngangs in full.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ལ་ བག་ཆགས་ ཡིད་ ཀྱི་ ལུས་ བྱ་བ་ གཅིག་ ཡོད་ ཀྱིས༔ རྡོས་བྱས་ ཤ་ཁྲག་ གི་ ལུས་ ནི་ མེད་པས༔
sentences.l: To you, habitual-tendencies' mind's body so-called, one, there-is, but: matter-made flesh-blood's body, as-for, there-is-not-because:
sentences.i: What you have is a so-called mental body of habitual tendencies, not a solid body of flesh and blood. So
sentences.n: bag chags, 'habitual tendencies', are the traces past actions leave in the mind; the body of the bardo is made of them. yod kyis, 'there is, but': kyis after a verb runs on to what follows, like gis in 002, and here sets up a contrast; the other recension has yod kyi. rdos byas, 'made of coarse matter', is the print's spelling of gdos bcas, 'material', of 002.

sentences.w: སྒྲ་ འོད་ ཟེར་ གསུམ་ གང་ བྱུང་ ཡང་ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ གནོད་པ་ མི་ འོང་ སྟེ༔ ཁྱོད་ ལ་ འཆི་རྒྱུ་ མེད་དོ༔
sentences.l: Sound, light, rays, three, whatever happened though, to you harm not comes, and: to you dying there-is-not.
sentences.i: whatever sounds, lights and rays come, they cannot harm you. You cannot die.
sentences.n: gang byung yang, 'whatever comes'. gnod pa, 'harm'. 'chi rgyu, 'something to die': rgyu after a verb is 'cause, occasion for'.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པ་ ཀྱང་ གིས་ ཆོག་གོ༔ བར་དོ་ ཡིན་པར་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: You-yourself's as-self-appearance face-knowing even by(?) suffices. The between it-is knowing do!
sentences.i: It is enough to recognise them as your own appearance. Know that this is the bardo.
sentences.n: ngo shes pa kyang gis chog go, 'by recognising alone it is enough', is awkward: kyang gis do not go together, and the other recension has ngo shes pas kyang chog, 'it is enough just by recognising'. The print is kept, and its sense is taken to be the same. chog go, 'it will do', as in 002. gyis cig is gyis shig, 'do!'.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ་ ད་ལྟ་ རང་སྣང་དུ་ ངོ་ མ་ ཤེས་ ན༔ མི་ཡུལ་དུ་ བསྒོམ་སྒྲུབ་ ཇི་ལྟར་ བྱས་ ཀྱང་༔ ད་ལྟའི་ གདམས་པ་ འདི་ དང་ མ་ འཕྲད་ ན༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family, now, as-self-appearance face not know if; in-the-human-land meditation-practice however done though, the present's instruction this with not met if:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, if you do not now recognise them as your own appearance, and if, however much you meditated and practised in the human world, you have not met this present instruction,
sentences.n: mi yul, 'the land of humans', the world of the living. bsgom sgrub, 'meditation and practice'. 'phrad, 'to meet': the instruction has to reach him now, whatever he did in life.

sentences.w: འོད་ ཀྱིས་ འཇིགས་སོ༔ སྒྲས་ དངངས་སོ༔ ཟེར་ གྱིས་ སྐྲག་གོ༔ གདམས་བའི་ གནས་ འདི་ མ་ ཤེས་ ན་ སྒྲ་ འོད་ ཟེར་ གསུམ་ ངོ་ མ་ ཤེས་ ན་ འཁོར་བར་ འཁྱམ་མོ༔
sentences.l: By-the-light you-fear. By-the-sound you-are-terrified. By-the-rays you-are-frightened. Instruction's point this not know if, sound, light, rays, three, face not know if, in-saṃsāra you-wander.
sentences.i: you will be afraid of the lights, terrified by the sounds, frightened by the rays. If you do not know this point of the instruction and do not recognise the sounds, lights and rays, you will wander in saṃsāra.
sentences.n: The three fears again, each with its cause marked by -s, 'by': 'od kyis, sgras, zer gyis. gdams ba'i is the print's spelling of gdams pa'i; gnas, 'place, point', where the other recension has gnad, 'key point'. The two conditions with na follow each other with no link. 'khyam mo, 'wanders', is a form of 'khyams.

sentences.w: ཀྱཻ་ རིགས་ཀྱི་བུ༔ ཞག་ ཕྱེད་ དང་ བཞིའི་ བར་དུ་ བརྒྱལ་ ནས་ འགྲོ་ སྟེ༔ བརྒྱལ་ བསངས་པ་ དང་ ང་ ལ་ ཅི་ བྱུང་བ་ སྙམ་བའི་ སྣང་བ་ འབྱུང་ སྟེ༔
sentences.l: O child-of-noble-family! Days half-and-four's until, having-fainted, goes, and: the faint cleared as-soon-as, 'To-me what happened?' thinking's appearance occurs, and:
sentences.i: O child of noble family, you lie unconscious for three and a half days. As soon as you come out of the faint, the thought comes to you, 'What has happened to me?'
sentences.n: zhag phyed dang bzhi, 'three and a half days', as in 002. brgyal nas 'gro, 'goes fainted'. bsangs, 'cleared': brgyal bsangs pa, 'the faint has cleared'. dang after a verb is 'as soon as', as in 002. nga, 'I', the plain word. snyam ba'i is the print's spelling of snyam pa'i, 'thinking'.

sentences.w: ཁྱོད་ ཀྱི་ བར་དོར་ ངོ་ ཤེས་པར་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: Yours, as-the-between face-knowing do!
sentences.i: Recognise this as your bardo.
sentences.n: bar dor, 'as the bardo': -r marks what a thing is recognised as, like sangs rgyas su in 002.

sentences.w: དེའི་ ཚེ་ འཁོར་བའི་ རུ་ལོག་ ནས༔ སྣང་བ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ འོད་ དང་ སྐུ་རུ་ འཆར་རོ༔ ནམ་མཁའ་ ཐམས་ཅད་ ཁ་དོག་ མཐིང་ཁར་ འཆར་རོ༔
sentences.l: That's time, saṃsāra's camp having-turned-back(?): appearances all as-light and bodies dawn. Sky all colour as-blue dawns.
sentences.i: At that time the course of saṃsāra turns back, and everything that appears dawns as lights and divine forms. The whole sky dawns deep blue.
sentences.n: ru log is uncertain: ru is a camp or a division of troops, and ru log, 'the camp turns back', seems to say that the course of saṃsāra is reversed; the sense given is a guess. sku ru, 'as bodies': ru is the 'as' ending after a vowel, like -r; sku, 'body', is the respectful word, used for the forms of buddhas and deities. The print writes nam at the head of p. 34 as ན with a small circle for m (ནཾ); it is written out. mthing kha, 'deep blue', is the print's spelling of mthing ga; with -r, 'as blue'. The other recension has 'od dang kha dog mthing gar, 'as blue light and colour'.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ དབུས་ཕྱོགས་ ཐིག་ལེ་བརྡལ་བའི་ ཞིང་ཁམས་ ནས༔ བཅོམ་ལྡན་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ སྐུ་མདོག་ དཀར་པོ་ སེངྒེའི་ ཁྲི་ ལ་ བཞུགས་པ༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, the centre-direction, Spread-Drop's realm from: the Blessed-One Vairocana, body-colour white, lion's throne on seated,
sentences.i: At that time, from the central realm called the Spreading Drop, the Blessed One Vairocana, white in colour, seated on a lion throne,
sentences.n: Here the first day begins: on each day one of the five buddhas appears. Rnam par snang mdzad, 'He Who Makes Appear in Every Way', is Vairocana, the buddha of the centre. bcom ldan, 'Blessed One', is a short form of bcom ldan 'das, the title of a buddha, which comes in full at the end of this part. Thig le brdal ba, 'the spread-out drop', is the name of his pure realm (zhing khams, 'field-realm'); thig le is 'drop, sphere' and brdal 'spread out', and the name is rendered word by word. sku mdog, 'body colour', the respectful word. The other recension adds mthing ka, 'blue', to the realm.

sentences.w: ཕྱག་ ན་ འཁོར་ལོ་ རྩིབས་ བརྒྱད་ བསྣམས་པ༔ ཡུམ་ ནམ་མཁའི་དབྱིངས་ཕྱུག་མ་ དང་ ཞལ་སྦྱར་ ནས་ རང་ ལ་ འཆར་དུ་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: Hand in, wheel spokes eight holding, the mother Sky's-Expanse-Lady with face-joined, then, oneself to dawning comes.
sentences.i: holding an eight-spoked wheel in his hand, in union with his consort, the Lady of the Expanse of Space, will dawn before you.
sentences.n: phyag, 'hand', and bsnams, 'held', are respectful words. yum, 'mother', is a buddha's female partner; zhal sbyar, 'faces joined', is their union. Nam mkha'i dbyings phyug ma, 'Lady of the Expanse of Space' (dbyings, 'expanse'; phyug ma, 'rich one, mistress'), is the consort of Vairocana. The print writes nam mkha'i contracted (ནམཁའི) and, at the line end, dbyings with a small s under the nga (དབྱིངྶ); both are written out. rang la, 'to oneself', is 'to you'.

sentences.w: རྣམ་པར་ཤེས་པའི་ ཕུང་པོ་ གནས་སུ་ དག་པ༔ འོད་ མཐིང་ཁ་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཁ་དོག་ མཐིང་ཁ༔ གསལ་ ལ་ དྭངས་པ༔
sentences.l: Consciousness's aggregate, in-its-place pure: light blue, the dharma-expanse's wisdom, colour blue, bright and clear,
sentences.i: The aggregate of consciousness, pure in its own place, is the blue light, the wisdom of the expanse of reality: blue in colour, bright and clear,
sentences.n: rnam par shes pa'i phung po, 'the heap of consciousness', is the fifth of the five aggregates (phung po, Sanskrit skandha) that make up a person; on each day one aggregate shows in its pure form as a buddha's light. gnas su dag pa, 'pure in its place'; the other recension has dag pas, 'because it is pure'. chos kyi dbyings, 'the expanse of things' (Sanskrit dharmadhātu), is reality as the space in which all things are; its ye shes, 'wisdom', is the first of five, the wisdom of Vairocana.

sentences.w: བཀྲག་ ལ་ མཆོར་བ་ གཅིག་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཡབ་ཡུམ་ གྱི་ ཐུགས་ཀ་ ནས་ ཁྱོད་རང་ གི་ མདུན་དུ་ མིག་ གིས་ མི་ བཟོད་པ་ ཙམ་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: lustrous and splendid, one, Vairocana father-mother's heart from, you-yourself's in-front, eye by not bearable as-much-as, piercing comes.
sentences.i: a lustrous, splendid light, it comes piercing from the heart of Vairocana and his consort to the space before you, so bright that your eyes can hardly bear it.
sentences.n: The print has སྐྲག, 'fear', a misprint for བཀྲག, 'lustre', corrected here: the light is being described, and the other recension has bkrag la 'tsher ba. The print swaps skrag and bkrag three times on these two pages. mchor ba, 'beautiful, splendid', is kept, though the other recension has 'tsher ba, 'shimmering'. yab yum, 'father-mother', is the buddha and his consort in union. thugs ka, 'heart', the respectful word. mig gis mi bzod pa tsam du, 'to the point that the eye cannot bear it'. zug, 'to pierce, to stab'.

sentences.w: དེ་ དང་ མཉམ་དུ་ ལྷའི་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ ཅིག་ ཀྱང་ མདུན་དུ་ ཟུག་ ནས་ འོང་ངོ༔
sentences.l: That with together, the gods' light, white, lustreless, one, also, in-front piercing comes.
sentences.i: Together with it a dull white light, the light of the gods, also comes piercing before you.
sentences.n: The print has སྐྲག་མེད, 'fearless', a misprint for བཀྲག་མེད, 'lustreless, dull', corrected here: the print itself writes bkrag med for this same light just below, and so does the other recension. lha'i 'od, 'the light of the gods': each bright wisdom light comes with a dull light from one of the six realms of rebirth, here the realm of the gods. The print writes 'ong ngo at the line end as one syllable (འོངོ); it is written out. In the other recension this light dawns alongside the blue one instead of piercing toward him.

sentences.w: དེའི་ དུས་སུ་ ཁྱོད་ ལས་ངན་ གྱིས་ དབང་ གིས་ འོད་ མཐིང་ཁ་ བཀྲག་ དང་ ལྡན་པ་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ འཇིགས་པ་ དང་ སྐྲག་པ་ སྐྱེས་ ནས་ བྲོས་ ཤིང༔
sentences.l: That's time-at, you, bad-karma by(?) power by, light blue, lustre with endowed, the dharma-expanse's wisdom, that, at, you, fear and terror having-arisen, fled, and:
sentences.i: At that time, driven by your bad karma, you will be afraid and terrified of that blue light, the lustrous wisdom of the expanse of reality, and flee from it,
sentences.n: las ngan gyis dbang gis has two 'by' endings where one expects las ngan gyi dbang gis, 'by the power of bad karma', as the other recension has it; the print is kept and read so. bkrag dang ldan pa, 'endowed with lustre'. bros, 'fled', past of 'bros. shing, 'and', joins this to what follows.

sentences.w: ལྷའི་ འོད་ དཀར་པོ་ བཀྲག་མེད་ དེ་ ལ་ ཁྱོད་ དགའ་བའི་ འདུ་ཤེས་ ནས་ འོང་ གི༔
sentences.l: The gods' light, white, lustreless, that, toward, you, delight's notion from, come, and:
sentences.i: and you will take delight in the dull white light of the gods and go toward it.
sentences.n: 'du shes, 'notion, perception'. The print has no verb before nas, so nas is read as 'from': 'you come out of a notion of delight'. The other recension has 'du shes skyes nas, 'a notion of delight having arisen'; the sense is the same. 'ong gi, 'comes, and': gi after a verb runs on.

sentences.w: དེ་ཙ་ན་ ཁྱོད་ འོད་ མཐིང་ཁ་ གསལ་ ལ་ འཚེར་བ་ དྭངས་ ལ་ བཀྲག་ ཆེ་བ་ མཆོག་ གི་ འོད་གསལ་ དེ་ ལ་ མ་ དངངས་ཤིག༔ མ་ སྐྲག་པར་
sentences.l: At-that-time, you, light blue, bright and shimmering, clear and lustre great, supreme's clear-light, that, at, not be-terrified! Not frightened-way:
sentences.i: At that time do not be terrified of the blue light, bright and shimmering, clear and full of lustre, the supreme clear light; do not be afraid.
sentences.n: The print has མ་བཀྲག་པར, 'without lustre', a misprint for མ་སྐྲག་པར, 'without fear', corrected here: it belongs to the prohibitions, and the other recension has ma skrag par. In the print, ma skrag par comes after the ༔ and opens the next sentence, where it has no verb to go with (that sentence ends in yin no, 'it is'); the other recension ends the sentence with it, and the translation reads it so. bkrag che ba, 'great in lustre'.

sentences.w: དེ་བཞིན་གཤེགས་པའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཆོས་ཀྱི་དབྱིངས་ ཀྱི་ ཡེ་ཤེས་ ཞེས་ བྱ་བ་ ཡིན་ནོ༔
sentences.l: The Thus-Gone-One's light-ray, the dharma-expanse's wisdom so-called it-is.
sentences.i: It is the light of the tathāgata, what is called the wisdom of the expanse of reality.
sentences.n: de bzhin gshegs pa, 'thus gone' (Sanskrit tathāgata), is a title of a buddha. 'od zer, 'light-ray', is here one word: the radiance of a buddha. The other recension begins this sentence with de ni, 'that'; the print has no subject, and 'it' is supplied. The print closes the sentence with yin no; the other recension runs on with yin gyi, 'it is, and'.

sentences.w: དེ་ ལ་ དད་པ་ དང་ མོས་པ་ དུང་དུང་ གྱིས་ཤིག༔
sentences.l: That to, faith and devotion longingly do!
sentences.i: Turn to it with faith and devotion, longingly.
sentences.n: dad pa, 'faith'; mos pa, 'devotion, trust'. dung dung, 'longingly, ardently', a doubled word akin to gdung, 'to long for'.

sentences.w: བཅོམ་ལྡན་འདས་ རྣམ་པར་སྣང་མཛད་ ཀྱི་ ཐུགས་རྗེའི་ འོད་ཟེར་ ཡིན་ནོ་ སྐྱབས་སུ་ མཆིའོ་ སྙམ་པའི་ མོས་བ་ གྱིས་ ལ་ གསོལ་བ་ ཐོབ་ཅིག༔
sentences.l: 'The Blessed-One Vairocana's compassion's light-ray it-is; for-refuge I-go' thinking's devotion do, and, prayer obtain(?)!
sentences.i: Think with devotion, 'This is the light of the compassion of the Blessed One Vairocana; I go to it for refuge', and pray.
sentences.n: bcom ldan 'das, 'Blessed One', in full. thugs rje, 'compassion', the respectful word. skyabs su mchi'o, 'I go for refuge': mchi is the humble verb 'to go', used of oneself before the holy. snyam pa'i, 'thinking', closes the words of the thought, as in 002. mos ba is the print's spelling of mos pa. gsol ba thob cig is uncertain: gsol ba, 'prayer, request', with thob, 'obtain', gives no clear sense; the translation takes it, as a guess, for 'make the prayer'. Where the print has Vairocana alone, the other recension has Vairocana yab yum, 'father and mother'. The part ends here; the print line goes on with de nas bcom ldan, which begins the next part.
